title: POC weekly sync - reliability incident follow-up
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on follow-up for the 5xx/timeouts incident on 2026-06-11. Team reviewed timeline, initial root cause hypothesis (bursting + KV cache eviction + retry storms), mitigations applied (tuned retries, increased connection/timeouts), and next steps for deeper logs, load test, and configuration changes for production pilot.
next_steps: Redwood SE to share per-request traces and aggregated 5xx logs by host (link + timestamp) - due 2026-06-14
BrightGuide SRE to run controlled load test with 10k qps burst to reproduce - target window 2026-06-16
Decision on short-term fix: increase client timeout to 45s and enable exponential backoff with jitter - actioned by BrightGuide devs by 2026-06-13
Schedule technical deep-dive with infra team for autoscaling tuning if issue reproduces - Redwood to propose slots 2026-06-17/18
action_items: Priya Patel (Redwood SE): export request traces and stack traces for 2026-06-11 03:12-03:30 UTC, upload to shared folder - due 2026-06-14
Miguel Torres (BrightGuide SRE): run the synthetic burst test with the provided harness and share results + Grafana links - due 2026-06-16
John Miller (AE): send updated pricing note for Dedicated burst capacity and SLA options - due 2026-06-14
Lena Chu (CSM): schedule the deep-dive and invite product/infra owners - due 2026-06-15
transcript:
[00:00] John Miller: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. We'll keep to 40 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Sarah Lee: Sarah here, Miguel and Priyanka on as well.
[00:09] John Miller: Great. The agenda is incident follow-up from yesterday's 5xx spike, current mitigations, and next steps. Priya, can you kick off with the timeline?
[00:18] Priya Patel: Yeah, sure. So on 2026-06-11 approx 03:12 UTC we saw a sudden jump in 5xx responses across a subset of hosts, mostly during a high-concurrency window. The first alerts were router-level 502/504s, then our infra saw elevated CPU and a lot of in-flight KV cache misses.
[00:35] Miguel Torres: Just to add, from our side the client perceived timeouts at around 03:14 UTC, and then we triggered retries which I think amplified the issue, we saw a retry stampede.
[00:42] Priya Patel: Yeah, that matches. There's likely a combination: burst of requests, some hosts hit memory pressure causing slower token generation, KV cache eviction causing regen of cached prefixes, and then retries from the client stacks creating new load.
[00:58] Priyanka Rao: Do we have a theory on whether this was application-level (prompt explosion) vs. underlying kernel selection mismatch?
[01:04] Priya Patel: Early hypothesis is infrastructure-level with eviction. We saw a correlated increase in seq-length for a small percentage of the requests - some long prompts that stretch memory - but the main signal was the cache miss rate and subsequent CPU spikes on a handful of GPUS.
[01:18] John Miller: Important to note we were running the hosted config with continuous batching and prefix cache enabled; dedicated pinning wasn't in place for this group.
[01:25] Sarah Lee: Right our prod pilot is hosted for now — we haven't moved to Dedicated. Would pinning have helped?
[01:30] Priya Patel: Pinning via Dedicated would give you predictable isolation and avoid noisy neighbor issues. But the immediate mitigation we applied was to increase server-side concurrency limits on the pool we control and reduce batch timeout to avoid overly large batches that cause OOM on longer sequences.
[01:45] Miguel Torres: Can you explain the batch timeout change again? I thought larger batches are cheaper.
[01:50] Priya Patel: Absolutely — larger batches are cheaper and more efficient but when prompt lengths vary a lot a large batch can push memory past the host's capacity. We lowered the batching window to favor smaller, quicker batches which reduces peak memory even if it's slightly less efficient.
[02:06] John Miller: We also adjusted the retry policy at the ingress — added exponential backoff with jitter and limited max retries to 2 to avoid retry storms.
[02:13] Priyanka Rao: Did you see any change after those mitigations?
[02:16] Priya Patel: Yes, after the config change we saw 5xx rate drop to baseline within ~7 minutes. But there were a few residual timeouts for long-running inferences.
[02:26] Miguel Torres: On our side we temporarily bumped client timeouts from 20s to 45s and that reduced visible user errors, but we want to avoid masking the underlying issue.
[02:34] John Miller: Good call. We also disabled one optimization path for the model that is sensitive to variable sequence lengths — that removed a kernel selection edge-case.
[02:44] Sarah Lee: That makes sense. Any logs or traces we can look at for the period?
[02:48] Priya Patel: Priya: I'll export the per-request traces and a consolidated 5xx CSV. I'll upload to the shared folder and paste links in the notes. There's also a short sample of the failing request IDs.
[02:58] John Miller: Fantastic. Miguel, were you able to reproduce locally with your harness?
[03:02] Miguel Torres: Not yet, we tried earlier but couldn't reproduce the exact pattern — our synthetic runs didn't include the same distribution of long prompts and the same concurrency burst. We'll run a targeted 10k qps short burst to try and hit similar pressure points as you suggested.
[03:13] Priya Patel: When you run it, please include the sequence length distribution I shared in the spreadsheet — focusing on the 95th percentile which spiked during the incident.
[03:23] Priyanka Rao: Curious — is there a way for us to get alerting at the request-id level before things escalate? We got host metrics but not enough request-level signals.
[03:31] Priya Patel: We have request-level traces and we can add a Prometheus-based alert for request-level 5xx rate per pool. That will give you finer granularity.
[03:38] John Miller: Also, consider configuring circuit breaker thresholds so the client can fail fast for a short window rather than retrying. That prevents downstream amplification.
[03:45] Miguel Torres: Agree. We'll plan to add the circuit breaker and reduce retries.
[03:49] Sarah Lee: On the business side, if this recurs we need runway to switch to Dedicated for the pilot. What's the lead time?
[03:55] John Miller: For Dedicated reserved capacity there is some provisioning time but we can provide short-term burst options with slightly higher cost within hosted while you finalize. I'll send pricing options after the call.
[04:04] Priya Patel: One more technical note — we saw some transient 502s at the load balancer layer because upstream pooled connections were getting exhausted. We recommended increasing pool size on the proxy and using connection keepalive where possible.
[04:16] Miguel Torres: Good to know. We'll check our client HTTP pool configs.
[04:19] John Miller: Let's recap next steps quickly and owners. Priya will upload traces and 5xx logs. Miguel will run the synthetic burst test. Sarah and team will change timeouts and enable circuit breaker. John will send Dedicated pricing and Jenna — sorry Lena — will schedule the deep-dive.
[04:32] Lena Chu: I'll send calendar invites for proposed slots, and I'll include the infra folks from Redwood and BrightGuide.
[04:36] Priya Patel: Quick question — do you want us to enable a temporary rule that drops ultra-long requests above a certain token threshold while you run the pilot?
[04:44] Priyanka Rao: We might, but prefer to try client-level controls first. If we can't stabilize we'll consider that option.
[04:50] John Miller: Sounds good. Anything else from BrightGuide?
[04:52] Miguel Torres: One last ask — can Redwood share the config diff for the batch/timeout changes so we can mirror them in our dev cluster?
[04:59] Priya Patel: Yep, I'll paste the diff in the shared doc and include recommended values.
[05:04] Sarah Lee: Thanks everyone, appreciate the quick turnaround on this.
[05:07] John Miller: Thanks all. We'll follow up on the action items, upload artifacts, and reconvene after the burst test.
[05:12] (meeting ends)
